newsitem.title: USA: USF&G to buy Mexican surety bond company.
newsitem.headline: USF&G to buy Mexican surety bond company.

text.p: USF&G Corp said it would acquire Mexico's Afianzadora Insurgentes Serfin in a move that would make it the largest surety bond operation in the world.
USF&G is paying Grupo Financiero Serfin SA de CV $65 million for Afianzadora, the largest surety company in Mexico. The Mexican company is expected to generate $40 million of premiums this year.

"This transaction exemplifies our strategy to increase shareholder value by opportunistically acquiring high-value specialty businesses that augment our core insurance operations," USF&G chief executive Norman Blake Jr said.
"In capitalizing upon USF&G's domestic leadership in surety bonding, we effectively enter this international market having superior growth potential as its number one player," Blake said.
Afianzadora, whose operations will not undergo any change, will report to USF&G Surety Group president Robert Lamendola.
The combined USF&G/Afianzadora surety operations are expected to produce over $200 million in direct premiums in 1996.
